design_notes: XlsxSnapshot.opc retains every OPC part verbatim (D2 ground rule), including xl/workbook.xml's raw bytes, so this is a full-depth subset (like pdf 1.7 ✳️a), not a schema-gapped one: Strict vs Transitional is directly checkable from workbook.xml's own xmlns/xmlns:r/conformance attributes plus package content types -- no honest-schema-gap diagnostic needed.

Checks (both subsets): HARD spreadsheetml main namespace match, HARD officeDocument relationships (markup) namespace match, HARD workbook@conformance attribute consistency, SOFT worksheet part content-type declaration (ECMA-376 Part 1 §12.3.24). ✳️strict adds one more HARD check: no part may declare the legacy VML drawing content type (ISO/IEC 29500-1 Strict removes VML entirely) -- the 'VML rules' the roster brief calls out.

Builders stamp their dialect's namespace/conformance attrs onto an already-engine-built snapshot (real XML rewrite via the shared xml component, not a fabricated literal) so a 'conforming construction must build' test is possible for ✳️strict; documented that ArtifactPack::encode_pack always regenerates workbook.xml as Transitional-shaped (engine::encode_xlsx has no dialect parameter to thread through), so a ✳️strict artifact's post-round-trip SubsetValidator recheck honestly re-reports the conformance-attribute violation -- same documented scope cut as the PDF/A 1.7 ✳️a pilot's writer note, not a false positive.

Engine fix (in-scope: standard-level ⚙️engine file): decode_xlsx/sniff_xlsx_bytes previously only recognized the Transitional officeDocument/sharedStrings relationship TYPE URIs, which would have made every genuinely ISO/IEC 29500-1 Strict-shaped package (whose relationship Type URIs are also purl.oclc.org variants per the Strict Annex) fail to decode at all before either subset analyzer ever ran. Fixed additively (Transitional recognition unchanged) and covered with a new hand-built-package decode test.
